html: The Warlmanpa are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, in the dry country between the Tanami Desert and the Barkly region. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language is close to that of the Warlpiri, their neighbours to the southwest. Other neighbours were the Mudburra and Jingili to the north and the Warumungu to the east. Little was written about them before the 20th century, when cattle stations and the township of Tennant Creek drew many of them in.
